subject: Agriculture
title: Climate Change and New Pests
description: Learn Climate Change and New Pests in one minute.

hook.text: Every 1°C of warming lets insects eat 10–25% more crops. Warmer means hungrier—and more generations per year.

buildup.text: Cold winters kill overwintering pests. As winters warm, pest populations start the season larger.

discovery.text: Pests are moving poleward at 2.7 km per year, colonizing crops that never faced them before.

twist.text: Climate change also weakens plant defenses. Stressed plants produce fewer defensive chemicals.

climax.text: Models predict crop losses to insects could increase 50% by mid-century under current warming trends.

punchline.text: Warming feeds the pests and weakens the crops. A double hit.

quiz.question: How fast are pests expanding their range due to climate change?

details.summary: Climate change is expanding the range of crop pests and diseases into regions previously too cold for their survival. Rising temperatures, altered rainfall patterns, and increased CO2 are changing pest behavior, reproduction rates, and the effectiveness of existing control methods.
details.whyItMatters: Climate models predict pest-related crop losses will increase by 10-25% per degree of warming. Farmers face novel pests with no local management experience, and existing resistant varieties may lose effectiveness in changed conditions.
takeaways: Warming temperatures allow pests to expand toward the poles at 2-3 km per year
Higher CO2 reduces the nutritional quality of plants, causing insects to eat more
New pest-crop interactions are emerging as species ranges shift with climate zones

faq.question: How does climate change increase crop pest damage?
faq.answer: Warmer winters allow more pests to survive year-round. Higher temperatures speed insect reproduction, producing more generations per year. Heat-stressed crops are more vulnerable to disease. Changed rainfall patterns create conditions favoring different fungal and bacterial pathogens.

faq.question: Which new pest threats are emerging due to climate change?
faq.answer: European vineyards face new insect pests moving northward. Wheat rust strains are appearing in previously unaffected regions. Coffee leaf rust is climbing to higher altitudes. Fall armyworm has expanded rapidly, and new fungal diseases are appearing in warming temperate zones.
